shots.text: IKEA's famous flat pack started with a sawed-off table.
Gillis Lundgren was a designer at IKEA in Sweden.
As the story goes, he tried to fit a table in his car. It was too big.
So he sawed the legs off.
The table fit. And that small moment made IKEA rethink how furniture travels.
Shipping big, fully built furniture was a headache. It took up space, and things got damaged.
The table went on sale as the Lövet, with its legs in the box.
Customers finished the job at home. It caught on.
Today IKEA is famous for it.
And that little table is still around. IKEA brought it back as the Lövbacken.
A table that wouldn't fit in a car helped change how we all buy furniture.
